html:
An Arrernte painter from the MacDonnell Ranges of Central Australia, famous for watercolours of the red hills, ghost gums and wide skies of his country. He was the first Aboriginal artist to win wide fame in Australia.

He grew up at the Hermannsburg Lutheran mission west of Alice Springs. In the 1930s the visiting painter Rex Battarbee taught him watercolour, and his first show, in Melbourne in 1938, sold out. He painted in a Western style, but the places he chose were his people's country, full of meaning for him. His success started the Hermannsburg School of Aboriginal watercolour painters.

His life showed the limits placed on Aboriginal Australians. In 1957 he and his wife were among the first Aboriginal people in the Northern Territory granted full citizenship, which let them vote and buy alcohol, rights his relatives did not have. In 1958 he was jailed for leaving alcohol where a relative could take it. He died the next year. He met Queen Elizabeth II in 1954. See Australia.
sum: An Arrernte painter from the MacDonnell Ranges of Central Australia, famous for watercolours of the red hills, ghost gums and wide skies of his country. He was the first Aboriginal artist to win wide fame in Australia.
